0.long_answer: The disorder is known as absence of fingerprints-congenital milia syndrome, also commonly referred to as Baird syndrome. It is an extremely rare autosomal dominant condition that has been reported in only ten families worldwide. Individuals with this syndrome present with an absence of fingerprints, the occurrence of blisters, and the development of facial milia shortly after birth. The condition stems from mutations in a skin-specific isoform of the SMARCAD1 gene located on chromosome 4, which plays a role in the development of fingerprint patterns. This mutation disrupts normal skin development, leading to the clinical features observed in the disorder.
